edition.name: Migne, Patrologia Latina 5 (1844), via Latin Wikisource
edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: Incolae coelorum futuri cum Deo Christo Tenente principium, vidente cuncta de coelo. Simplicitas, bonitas, habitet in corpore vestro. Irasci nolite sine causa fratri devoto: Recipietis enim quidquid feceritis ab illo. Hoc placuit Christo, resurgere mortuos, imo, Cum suis corporibus, et quos ignis ussit in aevo, Sex millibus annis completis mundo finito. Vertitur interea coelum tenore mutato: Comburuntur enim impii tunc igne divino. Ira Dei summi ardet creatura gemendo. Digniores, stemmate et generati praeclaro, Nobilesque viri sub Antichristo devicto: Ex praecepto Dei rursum viventes in aevo, Mille quidem annis ut serviant sanctis et Alto, Sub jugo servili, ut portent victualia collo; Ut iterum autem judicentur regno finito. Nullificantes Deum, completo millesimo anno, Ab igne peribunt, cum montibus ipsi loquendo. In bustis et tumulis omnis caro redditur acto, Demerguntur inferno, trahunt poenas in aevo. Ostenduntur illis, et legunt gesta de coelo Memoria prisca debito et merita digno. Merces in perpetuo secundum facta tyranno. Omnia non possum comprehendere parvo libello. Curiositas docti inveniet nomen in isto.
pass_a_gloss: Inhabitants of future heavens with God Christ holding the beginning, seeing all things from heaven. Let simplicity, goodness dwell in your body. Do not be angry without cause with a devoted brother: for you will receive whatever you do from Him. This pleased Christ, to resurrect the dead, indeed, with their bodies, and those whom fire has burned in the age, when six thousand years are completed and the world is finished. Meanwhile, heaven is turned with changed tenure: for the wicked are burned then by divine fire. The creature groans, burning with the anger of highest God. More worthy, of noble stem and born, and noble men, with Antichrist defeated, living again in the age by command of God, for a thousand years, so that they may serve the saints and the Highest, under servile yoke, so that they may carry provisions on their neck; so that they may be judged again when the kingdom is finished. Those nullifying God, when the thousandth year is completed, will perish from fire, speaking with the mountains themselves. All flesh is returned to the tombs and graves, they are submerged in hell, they drag punishments in the age. Their deeds are shown to them, and they read the deeds from heaven, from ancient memory, due debt and worthy merits. Reward in perpetuity according to deeds to the tyrant. I am not able to comprehend all things in a small book. The curiosity of the learned will find the name in this.

pass_b_english: Future citizens of heaven will live with God Christ holding the beginning, seeing all things from heaven. Let simplicity and goodness dwell in your body. Do not be angry without cause with a devoted brother, for you will receive back whatever you have done from him. This pleased Christ: to raise the dead with their bodies, even those whom fire consumed in the age when six thousand years are completed and the world is finished. Meanwhile, heaven is transformed with a changed order, for the wicked are then burned by divine fire. Creation groans, burning with the anger of the highest God. The more worthy, of noble stem and birth, and noble men, with Antichrist defeated, will live again in the age by God's command for a thousand years, so that they may serve the saints and the Most High under a servile yoke, so that they may carry provisions on their necks; so that they may be judged again when the kingdom is finished. Those who nullify God, when the thousandth year is completed, will perish by fire, speaking with the mountains themselves. All flesh returns to pits and graves; they are plunged into hell, dragging punishments through the age. Their deeds are shown to them, and they read the deeds from heaven, from ancient memory, due debt and worthy merit. The tyrant receives perpetual reward according to his deeds. I cannot comprehend all things in a small book. The curiosity of the learned will find the name in this.
